deep.reconstruction: This page is the archival front cover (blue paper wrapper) of the Göttingen manuscript Cod. Ms. Riemann 21 and contains no mathematics. Its inscriptions are as follows. (1) Top left, in ink: the shelfmark 'Cod. Ms. Riemann 21'. (2) A printed and handwritten library slip: 'Auch als Mikroform vorhanden unter Sign.: MF/Cod. Ms. Riemann 21' ('also available as microform under shelfmark MF/Cod. Ms. Riemann 21'). (3) A faint red-pencil note in the centre-top, reading something like '95 Bl.' or '95 BC' followed by an illegible string. This is plausibly a leaf count or an accession or foliation note, but it cannot be read reliably. (4) Top right, an old printed-border label with a handwritten title, almost certainly 'Luftwellen' (air waves), the Roman numeral 'VIII' (a group number of the old Nachlass ordering) and the item number '21'. The title links the bundle to Riemann's work on finite-amplitude sound waves, published as 'Über die Fortpflanzung ebener Luftwellen von endlicher Schwingungsweite' (1860). That paper introduced what are now called Riemann invariants and characteristics for the 1D isentropic gas equations, and the formation of shocks (compression discontinuities). The cover itself, however, carries no derivation, formula or claim to reconstruct, check or attribute.
